extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, researchers, and peer reviewers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommended practices for making scholarly peer review more sustainable by reducing reviewer burden, streamlining workflows, expanding the reviewer pool, and regulating new tools (e.g., AI). Targeted at journals, publishers, editors, and the research community.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage portable peer review (PPR) and reuse of existing reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Biology actively encourages portable peer review (PPR), where manuscripts are considered on the basis of reviews received at journals from other publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the work meets editorial criteria, editors should contact the previous journal to confirm history, share reviews and, if possible, original reviewer identities. Staff editors and Academic Editors can arbitrate existing reports directly, avoiding or minimizing further peer-review and thereby streamlining the process for authors and reducing reviewer burden. A system that takes into account existing reviews reduces futile cycles of peer review and benefits authors and reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publishers should agree to share reports and reviewer identities (with consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Call on all publishers to agree to sharing reports and reviewers’ identities (with consent) with each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sharing reports and reviewer identities between publishers (when consented to) enables efficient transfer of review histories and reduces duplicate reviewing; this requires willingness across publishers and appropriate consent/confidentiality safeguards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt and support journal-agnostic pre-publication review platforms (e.g., Review Commons, PCI)
rubrics_metrics.description: Participate in platforms like Review Commons and Peer Community In that organize review of preprint manuscripts before journal submission, producing a Refereed Preprint (manuscript + reviewer reports + authors' response).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refereed Preprints can be transferred to repositories (e.g., bioRxiv) and submitted to multiple affiliate journals, and transferred between journals upon rejection. These initiatives omit the need for serial re-review and allow reviewers to assess studies on merits without submission-location bias, streamlining processes and reducing reviewer workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions should require and recognize peer review contributions
rubrics_metrics.description: About 85% of researchers consulted consider that institutions should require and recognize peer review contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review should be adequately valued similar to publications and technical expertise in hiring, promotion, and funding decisions, thereby incentivizing participation and timely submission of reviewer reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious about paying peer reviewers—risks and concerns
rubrics_metrics.description: Paying peer reviewers has been discussed but is unlikely to garner widespread support due to concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns include diminishing report quality, creating misguided motivation (monetary gain), and the possibility that publishers would increase prices to finance payments. These risks must be weighed against potential benefits before adopting payment schemes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict AI use in peer review: allow polishing only, require disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Biology does not permit the use of AI to review a paper; AI may only be used to polish the text of a review that has already been written, and this must be declared to editors and authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AI cannot replace critique, contextualization, or expert judgement. Additional issues include confidentiality and data protection when uploading manuscripts to generative AI tools; regulation of AI use is needed. Any use of AI for polishing must be declared according to journal policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand and diversify the reviewer pool (include underrepresented regions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expand the reviewer pool to spread workload and reduce regional bias by approaching scientists from underrepresented and 'emerging' regions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data show established regions (e.g., USA, UK) review more relative to outputs than emerging regions (e.g., China, India). Actively recruiting reviewers from emerging regions democratizes the process and alleviates excessive demands on a small pool of reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use ORCID and better identification to find and disambiguate reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: A more consistent use of ORCiD identifiers would aid editors in identifying suitable reviewers and disambiguating individuals with the same name during conflict-of-interest checks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ORCiD adoption helps editors locate qualified reviewers, verify identities, and manage conflicts, thereby improving reviewer selection efficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include and officially recognise postdoctoral researchers as reviewers; declare co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral researchers are a possible source of suitable experts often overlooked; group leaders should recommend postdocs and declare when they co-review with lab members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should invite postdocs directly where appropriate. Group leaders who lack time to review should recommend qualified postdocs, and must always declare co-reviewing, enabling editors to approach those co-reviewers directly in the future.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set realistic reviewer deadlines and offer reasonable extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal deadlines for reviews are often shorter than the median time to complete a report (~16 days); deadlines should be adjusted to be more realistic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS Biology requests reviews within two weeks and is willing to provide short extensions within reason. Journals should consider aligning deadlines with typical completion times or offer flexibility unless exceptional expedited processing is warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage preprinting to reduce urgency for rapid publication
rubrics_metrics.description: With preprinting, studies can be made immediately available to the community, reducing the pressure to achieve very short time-to-publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and editors might accept slightly longer publication timelines if it relieves reviewer stress and maintains review quality; preprints provide access while review proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be open to experimentation with novel peer review structures and initiatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Given appetite for overhauling the system, stakeholders should remain open-minded to experimentation with new peer review structures and initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review reform is unresolved; because scientists are problem-solvers, journals, publishers and the community should pilot and evaluate new models to identify sustainable improvements.
